title: Human skeleton: bones, joints and inner anatomy
description: Explore the conventional 206 adult bones, axial and appendicular skeleton, joints, compact and spongy bone, and blood-forming marrow.

questions.question: Why is the adult human skeleton usually counted as 206 bones?
questions.answer: The conventional adult count includes bones that have fused during development and six middle-ear ossicles. Individual counts can differ because accessory bones, variable sesamoids and fusion patterns vary among people.

questions.question: What belongs to the axial skeleton?
questions.answer: The axial skeleton contains the skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage. It supports the head and trunk and helps protect the brain, spinal cord, heart and lungs.

questions.question: What belongs to the appendicular skeleton?
questions.answer: The shoulder and pelvic girdles, arms and legs form the appendicular skeleton. These bones provide attachment and leverage for movement and connect the limbs to the axial framework.

questions.question: What is the difference between compact and spongy bone?
questions.answer: Compact bone forms a dense outer layer; spongy bone contains a lattice of trabeculae inside many bones. Both are living tissues, and marrow occupies spaces within bones.

questions.question: Where is blood cell production found in adult bones?
questions.answer: Red marrow produces blood cell precursors in selected adult bones, especially axial bones and the proximal ends of some long bones. Yellow marrow is richer in fat and has different activity.
